chase_cards.name: Tropical Present
chase_cards.why: The whole source slice is one Fan Club object: a tropical postcard/Special Card that rewards club participation and gives the catalog a tiny social machine rather than a normal set slot.

key_artists.name: Atsuko Nishida
key_artists.why: Bulbapedia credits Tropical Present to Atsuko Nishida, whose early Pokemon work repeatedly makes the franchise feel approachable: soft creatures, readable poses, and a sense that collecting is also a form of play.

claims.text: The local catalog models Pokemon Card Fan Club January 1999 as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Tropical Present at source index 079.
The local release row records January 1999 as the month-level release date for this Fan Club source group.

The local row and Bulbapedia raw source identify the distribution note as Pokemon Card Fan Club (January 1999), while the source row describes Tropical Present as a postcard / Special Card rather than a booster, deck, or standard set card.
Bulbapedia describes Tropical Present as a jumbo promotional card sent to Pokemon Card Fan Club members in January 1999.

Bulbapedia records Tropical Present as a Special Card with a Do Nothing text box and an effect that can grant the player 10 GET points, which ties the card back into Fan Club participation rather than tournament legality.
Bulbapedia credits Tropical Present to Atsuko Nishida.
Pokumon describes the Tropical Present art as featuring Hoppip, Mareep, Pichu, Pikachu, and Snorlax under a tropical/present motif.
Tropical Present matters because it shows the Fan Club not only mailing collectibles but also turning card ownership back into participation through GET points.

Agents should preserve Fan Club January 1999 route, Tropical Present name, postcard / Special Card / jumbo format, GET-point text, Atsuko Nishida credit, and non-equivalence with Tropical Mega Battle or Southern Islands tropical memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present: the Fan Club sends the island back
narrative.why_it_matters: Tropical Present is charming because it is not trying to be a normal card. It is a Fan Club object with a postcard body, a Special Card label, a tropical gathering of friendly Pokemon, and a little rules joke that can send GET points back to the person who received it. That is the assembly we care about: mail, club membership, participation points, Nishida's warmth, and an object that sits halfway between card, gift, and receipt. An agent should never flatten it into just 'tropical promo.' The format and route are the card.

card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Tropical Present is sweetly literal: the Fan Club gives the member a tropical present, and the card can give points back. It is part card, part postcard, part club machinery.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present: a postcard that gives back
narrative.why_it_matters: Tropical Present has the soft magic of early Pokemon infrastructure. It is not a chase because it attacks hard. It is a chase because it shows the Fan Club acting like a living system: a member receives a bright oversized/postcard object, Nishida fills it with friendly Pokemon, and the text loops the gift back into GET points. It is a little receipt from a club that wanted children to keep participating.
